thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: S&P 500, Dow On Track To Snap Win Streak As U.S.-China Trade Tensions Escalate

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: S&P 500, Dow On Track To Snap Win Streak As U.S.-China Trade Tensions Escalate
text:
By Sue Chang, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Nasdaq extends losses as tech stocks under pressure
U.S. stocks retreated Monday as investors once again fretted over trade-policy uncertainty as Washington prepared to press ahead with tariffs on $200 billion in Chinese imports even as China hinted at a new round of retaliation.
Where are the major benchmarks trading?
The S&P 500 was off 10 points, or 0.4%, to 2,894, with technology and consumer-discretionary sectors among the biggest losers.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 41 points, or 0.2%, to 26,112 after briefly moving into positive territory earlier, and the Nasdaq Composite Index fell 77 points, or 1%, to 7,932.
Read: Stock-buyback mania overshadows surging growth in capital spending (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-why-stock-market-investors-reward-buybacks-more-than-capital-spending-2018-09-17)
What factors are driving markets?
Trade tensions continue to be a primary driver for market action, and the issue has received renewed focus in recent sessions as the relationship between the U.S. and China shows signs of deteriorating.
On Friday, The Wall Street Journal reported that the Trump administration plans to announce new tariffs of around 10% on $200 billion worth of Chinese products (https://www.wsj.com/articles/trump-to-announce-new-tariffs-on-200-billion-in-china-goods-1537040325?) on top of billions of dollars of tariffs that have already been levied.
In response, China said it may decline (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/china-may-decline-new-trade-talks-with-us-2018-09-16) a White House offer for renewed trade talks if President Donald Trump carries out the tariff threat. "China is not going to negotiate with a gun pointed to its head," a senior Chinese official told the Journal.
Technology stocks -- including names like Amazon.com Inc., which is classified as a consumer-discretionary firm -- have been highly correlated to the trade issue, with investors worrying about the impact it could have on their supply chains and global demand prospects.
Broadly speaking, investors have largely shrugged off the trade issue, focusing instead on strong corporate profits and economic data, there is still a concern that the issue could escalate and have a pronounced impact on global economic growth.
Read:Trade-war fears loom large over stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trade-war-fears-to-loom-large-over-stocks-2018-09-14)
In the latest economic data, the New York Fed's Empire State index fell 7 points to 19 in September (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/manufacturers-grow-at-slower-but-still-rapid-pace-in-september-feds-empire-survey-shows-2018-09-17).
What are market analysts saying?
The Chinese products targeted by the U.S. government for higher tariffs include many for which the country has a dominant market share, according to economists at Capital Economics.
"Indeed, China is the source of more than half of U.S. imports of the products on the $200 billion list, so alternative suppliers will be hard to find. If the tariff rate is set at only 10%, the impact will also be largely offset by the renminbi's 6% fall against the dollar since the middle of June," said Mark Williams, chief Asia economist at Capital Economics, in a report. "The damage from the latest escalation of the trade conflict on China's economy will be small -- much less than 0.5% of GDP, even if policy is not loosened further."
"Trade is back at the forefront of the news, and tech is among the most impacted sectors" to this issue, said Chris Larkin, senior vice president of trading product at E-Trade Financial.
"Not only have tech stocks have a really nice run in 2018 -- meaning the prices are a bit rich and it's natural to see a giveback -- but they're international stocks with a lot of international exposure. A good chunk of their profits come from overseas markets, and that's being impacted with the tariff talk."
Related: Why the U.S.-China trade deficit is so huge (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-all-the-stuff-the-us-imports-from-china-thats-causing-a-huge-trade-deficit-2018-03-23)
What stocks are in focus?
All five of the so-called FAANG stocks were lower, with Netflix Inc.(NFLX) falling 2.7%. Apple Inc. (AAPL) fell 1.7% while Facebook Inc. (FB) lost 0.9% and Google-parent Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOGL) slid 0.8%.
Amazon (AMZN) dropped 2.3% after The Wall Street Journal reported that the e-commerce giant was investigating internal leaks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/amazons-stock-falls-again-as-market-cap-drops-by-60-billion-from-1-trillion-intraday-peak-2018-09-17) to root out fake reviews and other seller scams.
DowDuPont Inc. (DWDP) shares rose 0.7% following an announcement that Chief Executive Edward Breen will assume the top executive position (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dowdupont-ceo-edward-breen-to-assume-executive-chairman-role-at-specialty-products-spinoff-2018-09-17) at the specialty-products company that will be created next year as part of the conglomerate's yearslong plan to split into three entities.
Coca-Cola Co.(KO) rose 0.4% after it confirmed that it was considering opportunities (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/coca-cola-says-its-closely-watching-the-opportunities-in-cbd-infused-beverages-2018-09-17) in CBD-infused beverages, drinks that contain cannabidiol, the non-psychoactive ingredient in marijuana.
Tyson Foods Inc.(TSN) stock fell 0.7% after the company said Chief Executive Tom Hayes will step down for personal reasons (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tyson-foods-stock-falls-after-ceo-steps-down-2018-09-17) after about two years in the role.
Mersana Therapeutics Inc.(MRSN) shares sank 24% after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration lifted a partial clinical hold (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mersana-therapeutics-says-fda-has-lifted-partial-clinical-hold-on-cancer-therapy-trial-2018-09-17) on its phase I trial of its cancer treatment XMT-1522.
Shares of Cellectar Biosciences Inc.(CLRB) gained 1.4% after it won a rare pediatric designation for cancer treatment from the FDA.
Canopy Growth (WEED.T) shares rose 2.4%. The company said its Tweed Farms Inc. site has received license amendments that approve remaining greenhouse space, expanding the company's licensed footprint (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cannabis-company-canopy-growth-wins-regulatory-approval-to-expand-production-2018-09-17) to about 3.2 million square feet.
Oracle Corp. (ORCL) shares rose 0.3%. The enterprise-software giant is scheduled to report its quarterly results after the market closes (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oracle-earnings-investors-brace-this-time-for-a-nebulous-reading-on-cloud-business-2018-09-14).
What are other markets doing?
European markets ended mixed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/hm-a-bright-spot-for-europe-stocks-as-dax-struggles-2018-09-17) and Asian stocks fell sharply (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-battered-as-trade-tensions-escalate-2018-09-16), pressured by the trade uncertainty and by a powerful typhoon (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/powerful-typhoon-leaves-trail-of-destruction-after-slamming-across-philippines-into-china-2018-09-16). The region was extending its recent weakness. Shares in Shenzhen have slumped nearly 30% so far this year, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index is down almost 20% from a recent peak.
Crude-oil prices (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-higher-on-supply-worries-2018-09-17) reversed direction to slide while gold settled slightly higher (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gold-gets-a-lift-from-wavering-dollar-stocks-2018-09-17). The U.S. dollar index fell 0.5% on trade jitters (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-adds-to-dip-as-trade-fears-are-back-at-center-stage-2018-09-17).
